summary: Richmond sprawls across 52.5 square miles along the northeastern shore of San Francisco Bay — making it physically larger than San Francisco itself — yet at roughly 2,169 people per square mile, much of that territory is open hillside, shoreline, and industrial land rather than dense neighborhood. The Chevron refinery, one of the largest on the West Coast, anchors the local economy and dominates the city's western waterfront, creating an unusual juxtaposition: world-class bay views and a 32-mile shoreline trail system sit within sight of one of California's biggest petroleum operations. A home-price-to-income ratio around 7.2× puts ownership in a zone that typically requires substantial savings or dual incomes, though that ratio is notably lower than many neighboring Bay Area cities, and the median rent of $1,895 remains below the regional average. BART connects Richmond directly to downtown San Francisco and Oakland, making it a genuine commuter hub, but motor-vehicle theft runs at roughly 1,088 per 100,000 — an infrastructure and enforcement challenge that shows up concretely in daily life. The mild, fog-modulated climate averages 66°F daytime highs year-round with nine hours of daily sunshine, meaning outdoor access along Point Richmond's bluffs or the Bay Trail is viable in every season. Richmond is a city where industrial legacy and bayfront beauty coexist in genuine, unresolved tension.
